name: BARBARA W. WEBB
description: Concurred, argued that State v. Sullivan was incorrectly decided as a matter of state constitutional law and that Gamble's arrest was proper because he committed a violation of law in the officer's presence.

name: BAKER, C.J.
description: Dissented, joined Justice Hudson's opinion.

name: COURTNEY RAE HUDSON
description: Dissented, argued that the majority improperly raised the issue of overruling State v. Sullivan sua sponte, violating the party-presentation principle and representing a fundamental shift in Arkansas jurisprudence that undermines fairness and objectivity in criminal appeals.

name: CODY HILAND
description: Concurred, argued that the General Assembly has the authority to amend voter-initiated laws under article 5, section 1, and that the word "section" in amendment 98, section 23(a) was a drafting error and should be read as "amendment."

name: BARBARA HALSEY
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: DON CURDIE
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: BAKER, C.J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: RHONDA K. WOOD
description: Concurred, argued that the General Assembly has the power to make legislative amendments to amendment 98, but overruling Arkansas Game & Fish Commission v. Edgmon was an unnecessary and advisory resolution.

name: SHAWN A. WOMACK
description: Concurred, argued that the General Assembly has the authority to amend voter-initiated laws and that "section" should be read as "amendment," but the case should have been reversed and dismissed solely on the basis of sovereign immunity.

name: HUDSON, J.
description: Not participating.

name: BRONNI, J.
description: Not participating.

name: NICHOLAS J. BRONNI
description: Concurred, argued that the Commissioner's August 2021 notice was reasonably calculated to inform BAS of the tax sale, satisfying due process, and thus sovereign immunity bars BAS's claims.

name: WEBB, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: KAREN R. BAKER, Chief Justice
description: Concurred in part, argued to reverse state claims due to sovereign immunity, but dissented in part, arguing that sovereign immunity cannot bar federal claims and issues of material fact remain for federal claims.

name: COURTNEY RAE HUDSON, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that sovereign immunity is not applicable when a plaintiff alleges unconstitutional state action and seeks injunctive relief, and that material facts remain disputed regarding the adequacy of notice.

name: SHAWN A. WOMACK, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that sovereign immunity should not bar federal claims due to the Supremacy Clause and that Article 2, Section 22 of the Arkansas Constitution provides an exception for state law claims regarding property rights.

name: COURTNEY RAE HUDSON
description: Concurred, arguing that the circuit court's gag order was an abuse of discretion because it was overly broad, vague, lacked a factual basis, and violated free speech and due process rights.

name: WOOD
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: WOMACK
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: HILAND
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: BRONNI
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: KAREN R. BAKER
description: Concurred, argued that the popular name and ballot title are intelligible, honest, and impartial, providing adequate and fair representation of the Proposed Amendment to voters.

name: WOOD, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion

name: WOMACK, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the ballot title was misleading because it did not explicitly state that a previously issued license in Pope County would be revoked and that the majority's interpretation went too far.

name: SHAWN A. WOMACK
description: Concurred, argued that the proposed amendment's popular name and ballot title were misleading because they suggested it was only about medical marijuana while also legalizing recreational use and altering constitutional amendment processes without clear disclosure.

name: DON CURDIE
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: BILENDA HARRIS-RITTER
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: CODY HILAND
description: Dissented, argued that the majority disregarded decades-long legal precedent regarding the sufficiency of popular names and ballot titles, and that the popular name and ballot title were not misleading when read together.

name: BAKER
description: Dissented with Justice Hiland.

name: WOOD
description: Dissented with Justice Hiland.

name: KEMP, C.J.
description: Not participating in the decision.

name: HUDSON, J.
description: Not participating in the decision.

name: CODY HILAND
description: Concurred, argued that the challenged Acts are constitutional and the lower court erred by applying strict scrutiny.

name: KEMP, C.J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: BARBARA W. WEBB
description: Concurred, argued that the lower court incorrectly applied strict scrutiny to election regulations, which should be reviewed under a rational-basis standard.

name: SHAWN A. WOMACK
description: Concurred, argued that the case should be dismissed based on Article 5, Section 20 of the Arkansas Constitution concerning sovereign immunity.

name: BARBARA W. WEBB
description: Concurred, argued that the legislative journals are the sole official record for determining if an emergency clause was properly passed, and the journals show it was.

name: KAREN R. BAKER
description: Concurred, argued that the lead opinion's sovereign-immunity analysis conflicts with prior precedent and that suits against the State are barred.

name: RHONDA K. WOOD
description: Concurred, argued that the case presents a nonjusticiable political question regarding legislative procedure, which violates separation of powers.

name: SHAWN A. WOMACK
description: Concurred, argued that the case should be dismissed solely based on sovereign immunity under article 5, section 20 of the Arkansas Constitution.

name: Special Justice CORY COX
description: Concurred with the majority opinion.

name: JOHN DAN KEMP
description: Dissented, argued that the case is moot because the LEARNS Act is already in effect and the public-interest exception does not apply.

name: HILAND, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: ROBIN F. WYNNE
description: Concurred, argued that the statute granting discretion to the Board of Election Commissioners was unconstitutional and the ballot title was sufficient.

name: Rhonda K. Wood
description: Concurred, argued that courts should limit their role in the ballot initiative process and trust voters to make informed decisions.

name: Shawn A. Womack
description: Concurred in part and dissented in part, argued that the statute was unconstitutional but the ballot title was misleading regarding child protection and the scope of changes.

name: Webb, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the ballot title was insufficient.

name: BARBARA W. WEBB
description: Concurred, argued that sovereign immunity does not bar writs of mandamus due to constitutional provisions, but it does bar declaratory relief because illegal/unconstitutional actions were not sufficiently pleaded, and subject-matter jurisdiction is lacking for APA claims.

name: Special Justice Emily White
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Baker, J.
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Robin F. Wynne
description: Concurred that sovereign immunity does not bar mandamus but dissented, arguing it should not bar declaratory relief as illegal acts were sufficiently pleaded, and the trial court has subject-matter jurisdiction for declaratory relief.

name: Shawn A. Womack
description: Dissented, arguing that the Arkansas Constitution's sovereign immunity provision (art. 5, § 20) bars the entire lawsuit against the State, including both mandamus and declaratory judgment.

name: Hudson, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: COURTNEY RAE HUDSON
description: Concurred, argued that the appellants' claims were speculative, hypothetical, and failed to demonstrate actual or imminent injury, thus lacking standing and being unripe and nonjusticiable.

name: Shawn A. Womack
description: Concurred, argued that while agreeing with the majority's disposition, Article 5, Section 20 of the Arkansas Constitution precludes this action against a State entity, suggesting the claims should be brought before the Claims Commission.

name: Barbara W. Webb
description: Concurred, argued that she agrees with Justice Womack's concurring opinion except for the assertion that Article 5, Section 20 of the Arkansas Constitution precludes the action against the State.

name: RHONDA K. WOOD
description: Concurred, arguing that the Attorney General has sovereign immunity for injunctive relief claims as plaintiffs failed to show ultra vires acts, and statutory immunity for individual-capacity illegal exaction claims as plaintiffs failed to allege malicious acts.

name: John R. Scott
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Shawn A. Womack
description: Concurred, arguing that the constitutional provision for illegal exactions allows citizens to sue the state, forming an exception to general sovereign immunity.

name: Karen R. Baker
description: Concurred with the majority's findings on sovereign and statutory immunity but dissented on the remainder of the opinion, referencing her position in a previous case.

name: Robin F. Wynne
description: Concurred on sovereign immunity and illegal exaction but dissented on statutory immunity, arguing it does not apply to injunctive relief claims against a state officer in her individual capacity.

name: Webb, J.
description: Not participating in the decision.

name: JOHN DAN KEMP, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court abused its discretion in granting the TRO because the parents failed to establish a constitutional rights violation or lack of district authority, and did not demonstrate irreparable harm.

name: Special Justice Howard W. Brill
description: Concurred with majority opinion.

name: Shawn A. Womack, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the case is moot due to the lapsed policy and that the substantial-public-interest exception is not fully satisfied, thus the appeal should be reversed and dismissed.

name: Barbara W. Webb, Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the circuit court's TRO should not have been reversed unless there was an abuse of discretion, and that the majority improperly delved into the merits of the case and undermined parental constitutional rights to make health-related decisions for their children.

name: Wood, J.
description: Not participating in the decision.

name: JOHN DAN KEMP
description: Concurred, argued that the circuit court had subject-matter jurisdiction over Solomon's due process claim, but not his equal protection claim, and remanded the preliminary injunction for further findings.

name: Karen R. Baker
description: Dissented, argued that the preliminary injunction should be reversed and dismissed based on prior precedent regarding sovereign immunity.

name: Shawn A. Womack
description: Dissented, argued that sovereign immunity bars the complaint against state entities, and the circuit court's order should be reversed and dismissed in its entirety.

name: ROBIN F. WYNNE
description: Concurred, argued that the statute is more substantive than procedural and therefore constitutional, not violating the separation-of-powers doctrine.

name: Rhonda K. Wood
description: Concurred, argued that the statute is constitutional because it is substantive, and would overrule Mendoza v. WIS International, Inc.

name: Mark Wankum, Special Justice
description: Concurred in judgment, argued that the foundational flaw in Johnson must be explicitly addressed and corrected.

name: Shawn A. Womack
description: Concurred in judgment, but dissented on the court's failure to explicitly abandon the bright-line rule of Johnson and its progeny.

name: Barbara W. Webb
description: Concurred that the statute is constitutional, but dissented on the court's failure to overturn Johnson and Mendoza precedents.

name: Kemp, C.J.
description: Not participating.

name: BARBARA W. WEBB
description: Concurred, argued that the statute unconstitutionally delegates legislative appointment power to private organizations not accountable to the people.

name: Karen R. Baker
description: Dissented, argued that the circuit court's finding that the statute was constitutional should be affirmed.

name: KAREN R. BAKER
description: Concurred, arguing that the circuit court did not abuse its discretion in finding that compliance with the statute's federal background check requirements was impossible, thus affirming the preliminary injunction.

name: COURTNEY RAE HUDSON
description: Concurred, delivering the majority opinion that affirmed in part, reversed and remanded in part, and dismissed as moot in part.

name: Barbara W. Webb
description: Concurred, argued that strict scrutiny is not the appropriate standard for reviewing the City's ordinance, which is a valid exercise of police power for public health and safety, and should be reviewed under a rational-basis standard.

name: Rhonda K. Wood
description: Dissented, argued that the case should not be remanded for further proceedings on as-applied constitutional claims because Convent failed to properly appeal, nonsuited claims, and the court should have ruled on the merits of summary judgment.
